comments.body:
**[INFO]** `return it->second->second;` returns a reference into the list node's stored string, but the caller receives `std::optional<std::string>` by value, so a copy is made — fine for safety, but means readers serialize on the underlying allocation anyway. More importantly, if `get()` is changed later to return a `string_view` or reference, the shared lock must be held for the lifetime of the returned view; document this hazard.

```suggestion
Add a comment noting the returned string is a snapshot and the lock is released after the copy.
```
